## Introduction

Bayesian variable selection for the HELIX pregnancy exposome [@vrijheid2014helix] and the
birth-weight z-score using an **Automatic Relevance Determination** (ARD)
prior [@tipping2001rvm]: each coefficient has its own precision `alpha_j`, so irrelevant
exposures are shrunk towards zero.

The model `linear_regression_ard` is in `src/models.jl`.

## Setup

The analysis runs in Julia [@bezanson2017julia]; `ExposomicsJulia` provides the shared helpers and models, together with DataFrames.jl [@bouchetvalat2023dataframes] and Turing.jl [@ge2018turing].

```{julia}
#| label: setup
using ExposomicsJulia
using Turing, ReverseDiff, LinearAlgebra, Statistics, DataFrames
using Arrow
DATA = joinpath(pkgdir(ExposomicsJulia), ".data")
```

## Data

Maternal covariates (BMI, weight gain, age) and the 57 pregnancy exposures
of the clean HELIX dataset.

```{julia}
#| label: data
df  = DataFrame(Arrow.Table(joinpath(DATA, "helix", "clean_dt.arrow")));
sel = vcat(["h_mbmi_None", "hs_wgtgain_None", "h_age_None"], names(df, Between(:h_abs_ratio_preg_Log, :h_thm_preg_Log)))
Xdt = Matrix{Float64}(df[:, sel])
Ydt = Array{Float64}(df.bw_zscore);
```

## Automatic Relevance Determination linear Bayesian regression

```{julia}
#| label: automatic-relevance-determination-linear-bayesian
m = linear_regression_ard(Xdt, Ydt)
```

```{julia}
#| label: automatic-relevance-determination-linear-bayesian-2
#| eval: false
reg_ard = sample(m, NUTS(; adtype = AutoReverseDiff(; compile = true)), 1000);
```

```{julia}
#| label: automatic-relevance-determination-linear-bayesian-3
#| eval: false
coeffs = chain_summary(reg_ard; quantiles = [0.025, 0.1, 0.5, 0.9, 0.975], pattern = "coefficients")
coeffs.parameter = sel
coeffs[coeffs.nonzero, :]
```
